# Policy-KB bijection audit — meter_testing_and_metering / task 0

Scope: the product is meter (Metering Service). Corpus: 59 published docs (docs_view sha256 b9b428d37d3a7c39…, checked equal title/content to docs/meter/*.json). The source is meter.extended.yaml together with task_tools.py. This task's policies are meter_ext_referee_backbill_settlement (root, on_request) and meter_ext_slow_meter_backbill (state_due). The base policies governing their subject (meter_accuracy_adjustment) are meter_accuracy_adjustment_rule, meter_test_result_rule (classification) and meter_test_request_rule (referee test, window, fee). The variant parameters read are test_method, accuracy_tolerance_pct, backbill_max_months, adjustment_threshold_usd, periodic_test_interval_years and referee_request_window_days. Entry conditions are met: policy-side round 2 PASS, check_docs DOCS OK, check_traceability OK (0.json 15/0) and the gate snapshot were all supplied. The audit rested on those snapshots and on the re-run at close-out below.

## source_to_kb

### meter_ext_slow_meter_backbill (hub doc_meter_slow_meter_backbill_desk_guide; baseline doc_meter_slow_meter_backbill_computation)
- **Rule head.** The source sentence "calculated for the company's own test result … latest test result taken by the test method of the meter's type, when that result classifies the meter slow … recorded on the meter's adjustment record against that test result, as a backbill, on the date it is calculated" is carried verbatim in the hub's opening paragraph. The hub adds the derivation "a result taken by a method other than the meter type's test method is not the company's own test for this purpose", which is entailed.
- **Baseline.** Bills are counted back from the company test date, up to min(reach-back, limit). Reach-back is half of the whole months from the later of installation and the latest WT result, rounded down. The limit is backbill_max_months. The charges are E + PSCR, corrected to full registration with factor |1 − 100/reg|. The result is rounded once, and anything below the threshold is recorded as 0.00. Steps 1–7 of the computation doc carry all of this, with the whole-calendar-month convention and a worked example. Defaults are stated. backbill_max_months and adjustment_threshold_usd are named as "the meter type's backbill limit" and "adjustment threshold", and both appear in figures in doc_meter_billing_adjustment_limits_by_meter_type. Nothing is added. No modifier hint.
- **slow_backbill_months_reached (method).** doc_meter_slow_meter_error_dating carries all three tiers: (1) failed-meter replacement or test exchange with no WT -> all months installation -> test; (2) WT on record and schedule effective after the latest WT -> months from the effective date; (3) otherwise "Neither dating applies". It also states that "after" is strict. The condition table matches the compute (tier 1 needs no WT; tier 2 holds regardless of the installation reason). The ladder is complete.
- **slow_backbill_limit (parameter).** doc_meter_slow_meter_backbill_limit_new_and_overdue carries 12 / 6 / 3. The new-meter period is counted from installation alone. The overdue count runs from the later of installation and WT, and the test is strict "exceed". Intervals are given per type in months (0/96/48/24). Complete.
- **slow_backbill_demand_basis (method).** doc_meter_slow_meter_demand_charge_correction carries all three tiers and the definition "billed at the minimum when its billing demand in kW equals the schedule's minimum billing demand". Complete. Cross-product: the tier reads the Electric Service Agreement's minimum billing demand and demand charge (service.yaml: GD 25 kW, 11.84 USD/kW). The doc names them in that product's words. The figures themselves are not on the runtime surface at audit time; see open note N3.
- **slow_backbill_target_registration (parameter).** doc_meter_slow_meter_correction_target carries the utility-initiated, periodic-only and neither tiers, the rule that "carried … whenever it was made", and the per-type targets table (98/99; IDM 99/99.5; PMI 99.5/99.75). Complete.
- **params.** new_meter_months 12, new_meter_cap_months 6 and overdue_cap_months 3 are all stated in figures.
- **prerequisite: []**. No document states a prerequisite for this policy. Correct.
- **Tool contract.** The hub's parameters, format and return line match the post_slow_meter_backbill_dc57beb1 docstring. The docstring's own "positive number … 0.00 records a backbill below the threshold" wording is carried as is. Owner is agent. Unlock/call path stated.

### meter_ext_referee_backbill_settlement (hub doc_meter_referee_backbill_settlement_acceptance; baseline doc_meter_referee_backbill_settlement_computation)
- **Rule head.** The definition of the dispute (company test slow by type method, referee = latest result, also slow) and the acceptance semantics (recorded as a backbill on the date the customer accepts; no acceptance means no settlement) are carried verbatim in the hub.
- **prerequisite → meter_ext_slow_meter_backbill**, form state, kind value_input. The policy_source "The referee backbill settlement is fixed only after the company test result it reviews carries its slow-meter backbill on the meter's adjustment record." stands verbatim in doc_meter_referee_backbill_settlement_acceptance and in no other document (string search over all 59 docs). The same-form restatement "while the meter's adjustment record shows no slow-meter backbill against the company test result under review, no settlement amount is fixed" sits in the same document. The connective "fixed only after" and the state form are intact. The basis for resolving the edge:
  - The depended-on hub doc_meter_slow_meter_backbill_desk_guide describes the write in the sentence's own words: "recorded on the meter's adjustment record against that test result, as a backbill".
  - The records (find_meter_adjustments) show no row on the meter.
  - The baseline's term "minus every backbill already standing on the meter's adjustment record" makes the value dependence visible.
  - The strength matches: a hard gate on the amount.
- **Baseline.** Carried in the computation memo, together with the inputs table and a worked example of the floor at 0.00. Complete. Nothing added.
- **Factors.**
  - settlement_months_reached: doc_meter_referee_backbill_error_dating, all three tiers plus the strict-"after" Q&A.
  - settlement_limit: doc_meter_referee_backbill_settlement_limit, 12 / 6 / 3, intervals, boundary pairs.
  - settlement_demand_basis: doc_meter_referee_backbill_demand_repricing, three tiers.
  - settlement_target_registration: doc_meter_referee_backbill_correction_target, three tiers plus targets table.
  - settlement_last_bill: doc_meter_referee_backbill_post_test_bills, removed-after, in-service, otherwise.
  Every ladder is complete with its figures.
- **params.** settlement_new_meter_months 12, cap 6 and overdue 3 are stated.
- **Tool contract.** accept_referee_backbill_settlement_27524241: owner user ("the customer themselves runs … with call_user_discoverable_tool"), parameters and return line match the docstring, including "on top of whatever backbill already stands for the meter".

### Base policies in scope
- **meter_accuracy_adjustment_rule** (doc_meter_accuracy_adjustment_rule). Clauses in force:
  - fast -> refund, slow / non-registering -> backbill
  - threshold -> 0.00 posts nothing
  - each result adjusted once
  - backbills attract no LPC
  - residential backbill may be placed in an arrangement
  All carried, plus the direction table. The **retired surface** (a) through (e) matches the declared overwrites one to one:
  - (a) period / error start: slow, referee, fast, referee-refund, NR
  - (b) corrected charges: slow, referee, fast, referee-refund
  - (c) amount and adjusted kWh: slow, referee, fast, referee-refund
  - (d) non_registering_basis: NR
  - (e) crediting on the service agreement: referee backbill, referee refund
  Each is written as "No longer in force". No undeclared retirement. No retired clause is stated as in force in this task's documents (see N1 for parameter rows).
- **meter_test_result_rule** (doc_meter_test_result_classification): classification with inclusive edges, one result per request, exchange within the type's period. Complete.
- **meter_test_request_rule** (doc_meter_meter_test_requests_and_referee_window + doc_meter_commission_referee_test_terms): customer of record, in-service only, scheduling, witnessing, referee window counted from the day after with the last day accepted, fee refunded if outside tolerance, periodic tests, LPC deferral. Complete. Figures: 30 days; fees 25 / 50 / 100.
- **Variant parameters read.** Checked row by row against doc_meter_accuracy_test_terms_schedule, doc_meter_billing_adjustment_limits_by_meter_type and the catalogue: test_method, tolerance, backbill_max_months, adjustment_threshold_usd, periodic interval, referee window. All six types match.

Untriggered branches checked as carried: test exchange; schedule dating; overdue limit; periodic-only target; neither target; no demand charge; meter in service; removal on or before the test; settlement floor at 0.00; threshold to 0.00.

## kb_to_source

Every normative sentence of the 13 documents of these two policies, plus the base documents above, traces to a source atom. Restatements that were checked as entailed rather than added:
- boundary tables
- "after is strict"
- "a periodic request also on record does not change a utility-initiated target"
- input-source tables
- worked hypothetical examples (recomputed: 26.25, 50.77 → 6.77, 0.0315789 / 0.0421053, 2,310.00, 22 months, 0.0206186 / 0.0257732)

Additions, rewrites or omissions found: **none**.

Prerequisite-side specific checks:
- (i) Cross-problem operational guidance ("if unmet, first call …"): none. Each of the six tool names appears only in its own hub (string search).
- (ii) A task's opening world state written as a policy fact: none. All examples are labelled hypothetical, and no document states that a particular customer or meter currently lacks a backbill.

Policy-side notes (reported, not counted against the documents):
- **N1 (orphaned variant parameters).** The variants still carry error_start_basis, adjustment_charge_basis, non_registering_basis, adjustment_rounding_rule and adjustment_rate_basis. Their only consuming clauses (base (a)–(d)) are overwritten. doc_meter_billing_adjustment_limits_by_meter_type renders them faithfully as "limits and bases that bound a billing adjustment", including the row "Charges corrected by an accuracy adjustment (all types) | Energy, demand and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges of each regular bill in the adjustment period". So the visible surface carries a second statement of the corrected charges next to the in-force slow-meter and referee baselines (E + PSCR). A careful reader resolves it through retired clause (b) in doc_meter_accuracy_adjustment_rule ("No longer in force: the corrected charges are the energy, demand and Power Supply Cost Recovery charges …"). The root cause is on the policy side: parameters were left live after their consuming clauses were overwritten.
- **N3 (cross-product figure visibility).** Every demand factor tier reads minimum_billing_demand_kw and demand_charge_usd_kw of the Electric Service Agreement product. No document of the runtime corpus states them. docs/ holds only budget, dr, medical, meter and nem. In this world the tier is recoverable from the bill rows (billing demand 25.0 kW against lower measured demand). This is the explicit cross-product coverage gap of this skill, to be re-checked once the Electric Service Agreement KB is published.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** Every atom of the two extended policies is carried in full, at the same strength: rule, baseline, all nine factor ladders, params, the prerequisite and both tool contracts. So are the in-scope base policies and the retired surface. No addition. N1 and N3 are policy-side and coverage notes, not KB-BIJECTION findings. First revision.

- The prerequisite sentence is verbatim on the blocked side only: doc_meter_referee_backbill_settlement_acceptance. Its same-form restatement and the records table row ("The slow-meter backbill standing against the company test result") are state descriptions in the same document. Neither names the depended-on tool, performer or route.
- The depended-on documents (slow-meter hub, computation and four factor docs) never mention the referee settlement. The depended-on side does not disclose who waits on it.
- No document aggregates prerequisites, strings problems into an ordered procedure, or carries a wrong/correct-reading contrast or a cross-problem FAQ. Searched by meaning plus pattern scans for "first/then/before/until", "unless", "see", "mistake", "most customers", "elsewhere": the only hits are the prerequisite sentences and base reading-rule text.
- Titles name general subjects. "Customer Care Note on Metering Service Referee Backbill Settlements" names the on_request policy's request type, which is allowed. None mirrors the bakery's situation.
- The slow-meter computation and referee memo computation documents contain no hint of modifiers. The factor documents do not say which tier customers fall on, name the computation document, or point at another factor.
- Findability: the slow-meter hub is reachable through the words of the sentence and the records: "slow-meter backbill", "adjustment record", "slow", "company test". The factor docs are reachable through record words: "failed-meter replacement", "utility-initiated test request", "minimum billing demand", "removed from service", "installed fewer than … months".
- Blind hop mark: P1 -> P2 state-derived.

**PASS** (no KB-EXPLICIT finding).
